items.why: along with 뒤는 부가 어구라 핵심 주어 leader(단수)에 was가 일치해요. 나머지는 각각 Each(단수), members(복수), A number of(복수)에 맞지 않아요.

items.q: 다음 중 병렬 구조가 어색한 문장은?

He wants to travel, to study, and to work abroad.
The soup was hot, salty, and delicious.
We cleaned the room, washed the dishes, and took out the trash.
items.why: enjoy 뒤의 항목은 동명사로 맞춰야 하므로 to play는 playing이어야 해요.

Please open the window, turn on the fan, and close the door.
The speaker was clear, funny, and with confidence.
I like swimming in summer, skating in winter, and hiking in autumn.
items.why: 형용사 clear, funny에 맞춰 with confidence도 형용사(confident)여야 해요.

items.q: 다음 중 주어와 동사의 일치가 틀린 문장은?
o: Economics is a required subject for first-year students.
The students in the back row were whispering during the film.
Neither the pilot nor the passengers were injured in the incident.

o: Every child in the program receives a free lunch.

The cost of the repairs was higher than we expected.
Mathematics and physics are required for this course.
items.why: there 뒤의 진짜 주어 stops가 복수이므로 There are이어야 해요.

items.q: 다음 중 병렬 구조가 올바른 문장은?
o: Teenagers need to sleep enough, eating well, and exercise regularly.
Teenagers need to sleep enough, eat well, and exercising regularly.
Teenagers need to sleep enough, eat well, and exercise regularly.
Teenagers need sleeping enough, to eat well, and exercise regularly.
items.why: need to 뒤에 sleep, eat, exercise 동사원형이 나란히 이어져요.

items.q: 다음 중 비교 대상이 논리적으로 같은 종류끼리 비교된 문장은?

The windows of the old house are smaller than the new house.
The windows of the old house are smaller than that of the new house.
The windows of the old house are smaller than it of the new house.
items.why: windows(복수)와 windows를 비교하므로 복수 대명사 those로 받아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
The software is easy to install, simple to use, and ___ to update.
items.why: easy, simple처럼 형용사를 나열하므로 quick이 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
The mayor is expected to announce a new budget, to meet union leaders, and ___ at the opening ceremony.
items.why: 앞의 to announce, to meet에 맞춰 to speak으로 이어요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
The company is known for its quality, its low prices, and ___.
items.why: its + 명사 구조를 세 번 나열해야 해요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Visitors may either walk along the coast or ___ a bicycle from the hotel.
items.why: may 뒤의 either A or B는 모두 동사원형이에요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Her speech was not long but ___.
items.why: not long(형용사)과 but으로 이어지므로 형용사 powerful이에요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
I would rather stay home than ___ in the rain.
items.why: would rather A than B에서 A, B 모두 동사원형이에요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
The new rules require drivers to wear seat belts and ___ their phones while driving.
items.why: require drivers to wear ... and (to) avoid ...처럼 to 뒤 동사원형이 이어져요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
He explained why the experiment failed and ___.
o: what the team should do next
what should the team do next
the team should do what next
what to do the team next
items.why: why절과 같은 의문사절 어순(의문사+주어+동사)으로 이어야 해요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Neither the film's plot nor its music ___ memorable.
items.why: neither A nor B는 가까운 B(music, 단수)에 일치시켜요.

items.q:

Both the book and the movie ___ popular among teenagers.
items.why: both A and B는 복수 주어이므로 복수 동사를 써요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
The instructions say to turn off the machine, unplug the cable, and ___ the lid before cleaning.
items.why: turn off, unplug처럼 명령형 동사원형을 나열해요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 핵심 주어를 골라 동사의 수를 정할 때, 동사 are 와 일치하는 명사는?
The effects of the new policy on small farms are still unclear.
items.why: 전치사구(of the new policy, on small farms) 안의 명사는 동사의 수를 정하지 않아요. 핵심 주어는 effects예요.

items.q: Either the guide or the tourists have to carry the map. 이 문장에서 have 는 어느 명사에 일치하는가?
items.why: either A or B에서 동사는 가까운 B(tourists)에 일치해요.

items.q: He plans to study law at a university, to travel widely in Asia, to learn two new languages, and working as a news reporter. 형태가 나머지와 다른 어구는?
o: to study law at a university
items.why: plans 뒤의 항목은 to부정사로 맞춰야 하므로 working은 to work여야 해요.

items.q: 다음 중 짝이 올바른 상관접속사 표현은?
items.why: neither는 nor, both는 and, not only는 but also와 짝이에요.

items.q: 'not only A ___ B'에서 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말은?
items.why: not only A but also B는 'A뿐만 아니라 B도'라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 'each of + 복수명사'가 주어일 때 동사의 수는 어떻게 맞추는가?

items.why: each가 핵심 주어이므로 of 뒤가 복수여도 단수 동사를 써요.

items.q: A number of 와 The number of 에 대한 설명으로 옳은 것은?
o: A number of는 단수 취급하고 The number of는 복수 취급한다
둘 다 복수 취급하며 뒤의 명사와 상관없이 복수 동사를 쓴다
둘 다 단수 취급하며 뒤의 명사와 상관없이 단수 동사를 쓴다
A number of는 복수 취급하고 The number of는 단수 취급한다
items.why: A number of는 '많은'이라는 뜻의 복수 취급이고, The number of는 '~의 수'라는 뜻이라 number가 주어(단수)예요.

items.q: 사무직 업무를 설명하는 문장 중 병렬 구조가 올바른 것을 고르세요.
o: The job involves answering calls, scheduling meetings, and organizing files.
The job involves answering calls, to schedule meetings, and organizing files.
The job involves answering calls, scheduling meetings, and file organization.
The job involves answering calls, scheduling meetings, and to organize files.
items.why: involve 뒤의 세 항목을 모두 동명사로 맞춰요.

items.title: Rooftop Bees
items.text: When Hana's neighbors first heard that the apartment building would keep bees on its roof, many of them objected. They imagined swarms in the stairwell, stings in the playground, and endless complaints from the landlord. The building's residents' committee, however, listened to every worry, invited an experienced beekeeper to answer questions, and agreed to a six-month trial. During that time, none of the feared problems appeared. The bees flew toward the city's parks, not toward the balconies, and the only visible change was a row of flowerpots that tenants planted to feed them. By autumn, the roof hives had produced enough honey for every household to receive a small jar. Several former critics now volunteer to help with the harvest. What changed their minds was not an argument but an experience: they saw that careful planning had turned a risky idea into a shared project.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why bees are disappearing from large modern cities
How to harvest honey safely without protective clothing
How a rooftop beekeeping plan won over doubtful neighbors
Why landlords should forbid unusual activities on roofs
qs.why: 처음에는 반대하던 이웃들이 신중한 계획과 시범 운영을 거쳐 생각을 바꾼 과정이 중심 내용이에요.

qs.q: What did the committee do before the project began?
o: It invited an expert to answer questions and set up a trial
It asked every tenant to sign a contract with the landlord
It moved the hives to a nearby park for the first winter
It bought flowerpots for the balconies of every household
qs.why: 위원회는 양봉가를 초청해 질문에 답하게 하고 6개월 시범 운영에 합의했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "objected" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 문맥상 이웃들이 양봉 계획에 반대했다는 뜻이므로 protested와 가장 가까워요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the former critics?
o: They still fear the bees but are too polite to say so
Their opinions improved after they saw the results themselves
They received larger jars of honey than other residents
They moved out of the building during the six-month trial
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 논쟁이 아니라 경험이 생각을 바꾸었다고 해요. 이들은 이제 수확을 돕는 자원봉사자가 되었어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer list "swarms in the stairwell, stings in the playground, and endless complaints"?
o: To prove that those problems actually happened in the end
To show the range of problems the neighbors had imagined
To compare this building with others in the same city
To explain how the committee solved each of the problems
qs.why: 나열된 항목들은 이웃들이 상상했던 문제들이고, 결국 어느 것도 일어나지 않았어요.

items.title: A Later Bell
items.text: Many teenagers struggle to wake up for an eight o'clock class, and scientists have an explanation. During adolescence the body clock shifts, so young people feel sleepy later at night and want to sleep later in the morning. A school in a small town tested a simple change: lessons began forty minutes later. Teachers reported that students arrived calmer, paid closer attention, and made fewer mistakes in the first period. Absences dropped, too. Not everyone was pleased, however. Bus drivers had to change their routes, and sports teams lost part of their afternoon practice time. Parents who worked early shifts worried about leaving their children alone at home. The principal admitted that the plan was not perfect but argued that the benefits for learning outweighed the costs. Other schools in the region are now watching the results closely before they decide whether to follow.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Teenagers should be allowed to choose their own class schedules each year
Sports teams are more important than early morning lessons for students
Bus drivers are the group most harmed by changes in school schedules
A later start brought learning benefits as well as practical difficulties
qs.why: 늦은 등교의 학습상 이점과 현실적인 어려움을 함께 보여 주는 글이에요.

qs.q: Which problem was caused by the new schedule?
o: Some sports teams had less time to practice
Many students began to miss more days of school
Teachers had to shorten every lesson in the morning
Bus companies refused to continue serving the school
qs.why: 방과 후 연습 시간이 줄어든 팀이 있었다고 해요. 결석은 오히려 줄었어요.

qs.q: Why are other schools "watching the results closely"?
o: They have already decided to copy the new schedule
They believe the plan has failed in the small town
They are not yet sure the change is worth making
They want to hire the principal as a consultant
qs.why: 아직 따라 할지 결정하지 않았다는 말에서 변화의 가치를 확신하지 못한다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "outweighed" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 이점이 비용보다 더 중요했다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which statement is NOT supported by the passage?
o: Students were absent more often after the change.
Students made fewer mistakes in the first period.
The body clock shifts during adolescence.
The principal admits that the plan has weaknesses.
qs.why: 결석은 줄었다고 했으므로 '더 자주 결석했다'는 진술은 지문과 맞지 않아요.

items.title: A Request for the Courtyard
items.text:
Dear Mr. Okafor,
I am writing on behalf of the Green Hands Club to request permission to use the school courtyard for a spring cleanup. Our members plan to remove litter, plant native flowers, and repair the wooden benches that rain has damaged. We expect about thirty students to take part on Saturday, April 12, from nine o'clock until noon. Because the work involves tools and soil, we would like at least one teacher to supervise. The club will buy all materials with money from last year's bake sale, so the school will not need to pay anything. If you approve, we also hope to display a short report about the project in the main hallway. Thank you for considering our request, and I look forward to hearing from you.
Sincerely,
Minseo Park, Club President

qs.q: Why did Minseo write this letter?
o: To report that a bench had been damaged by rain
To invite Mr. Okafor to join the club as a member
To thank the school for paying for the materials
To ask for permission to hold a cleanup event
qs.why: 글쓴이는 교정 안뜰을 봄맞이 청소에 사용해도 되는지 허락을 구하고 있어요.

qs.q: Who will pay for the materials?
o: The school, using its yearly budget
The club, with money from a bake sale
Mr. Okafor, out of his own pocket
The students, with a fee on the day
qs.why: 동아리가 지난해 베이크 세일에서 번 돈으로 재료를 산다고 해요.

qs.q: Why does the club want a teacher to be present?
o: The students are not allowed to enter the courtyard alone
The work includes tools and soil that need supervision
Mr. Okafor has asked to inspect every project
The report for the hallway must be signed by a teacher
qs.why: 도구와 흙을 다루는 작업이라 감독할 교사가 필요하다고 설명해요.

qs.q: Which activity is NOT in the club's plan?
o: Painting the walls of the main hallway
qs.why: 복도에 보고서를 전시할 계획은 있지만 벽을 칠한다는 말은 없어요.

qs.q: Which phrase best describes the tone of the letter?
qs.why: 정중한 인사와 구체적인 계획으로 쓰인 격식 있는 편지예요.

items.title: Life in the Tide Pool
items.text: A tide pool looks calm, yet life there is anything but easy. Twice a day, the sea retreats and leaves small basins of water on the rocks. Animals living in these pools must survive hot sunshine, sudden rain, and waves that crash against them without warning. Sea stars hold on with hundreds of tiny tube feet, limpets clamp themselves tightly to the stone, and crabs hide in cracks until the water returns. Even the water itself changes quickly: as it warms under the sun, it loses oxygen and grows saltier, a combination that would kill many ocean animals within hours. The creatures of the tide pool have adapted to this, which makes them valuable to scientists. By studying how they cope with sudden change, researchers hope to predict how other sea life might respond as oceans grow warmer.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why the sea leaves small basins on the rocks twice every day
Which sea animals are most dangerous to people visiting the shore
How tide-pool animals survive rapid changes in their surroundings
How scientists build artificial pools in laboratories for research
qs.why: 조수 웅덩이 생물들이 급격한 환경 변화를 견디는 방식과 그 연구 가치를 다뤄요.

qs.q: How do sea stars stay in place?
o: They clamp their shells tightly to the stone
They hide in cracks until the water returns
They hold on with many tiny tube feet
They float near the surface of the pool
qs.why: 불가사리는 수백 개의 작은 관족으로 달라붙어요. 삿갓조개와 게의 방식과 구분해야 해요.

qs.q: What happens to the water as it warms under the sun?
o: It holds less oxygen and becomes saltier
It becomes colder and holds more oxygen
It rises quickly and floods nearby rocks
It turns clear and attracts new animals
qs.why: 따뜻해지면 산소를 잃고 더 짜진다고 해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "cope with" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 급격한 변화에 잘 대처한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why are tide-pool creatures valuable to scientists?
o: They are easier to catch than most animals in deep water
They may show how other sea life will react to warmer oceans
They produce extra oxygen that helps to cool the ocean
They have never been affected by any change in the sea water
qs.why: 급변에 적응한 이들을 연구하면 바다가 따뜻해질 때 다른 생물의 반응을 예측할 수 있다고 해요.

items.title: The Price of Working at Home
items.text: Working from home has changed how people think about the office. Employees save hours of commuting, spend more time with family, and can often arrange their day to match their energy. Employers, meanwhile, save on rent and can hire people from distant cities. Yet the arrangement has costs that are easy to overlook. New workers miss the casual conversations through which experienced colleagues pass on unwritten rules. Creative teams find that brainstorming through a screen is slower and less spontaneous. Some employees also discover that, without a clear boundary between work and rest, they answer messages late at night and feel unable to relax. Companies that handle remote work well tend to set clear hours, schedule occasional meetings in person, and train managers to measure results rather than hours at a desk. In other words, success depends less on where people work than on how the work is organized.

qs.q: Which statement best expresses the writer's main point?
o: Offices will soon disappear from every large company
The success of remote work depends on how it is organized
Employees are always happier when they work at home
Managers should check their staff more often during the day
qs.why: 마지막 문장이 요지를 직접 말해요. 어디서 일하느냐보다 일을 어떻게 조직하느냐가 성패를 좌우해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "the arrangement" refers to
qs.why: 앞 문장들에서 다룬 재택근무 방식을 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why are new workers disadvantaged by remote work?
o: They miss informal chats where unwritten rules are shared
They are not allowed to join any official meetings
They must work longer hours than experienced colleagues
They receive less pay while they are learning the job
qs.why: 경험 많은 동료가 불문율을 전해 주는 가벼운 대화를 놓친다고 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about employees who answer messages late at night?
o: They enjoy working more than they enjoy resting
They have been told to reply to messages immediately
They find it hard to separate work from rest
They work for companies that set clear working hours
qs.why: 일과 휴식의 경계가 불분명하면 밤늦게 답장하고 쉬지 못한다는 내용에서 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which method do successful companies use, according to the passage?
o: Asking employees to keep their cameras on all day
Replacing in-person meetings with weekly written reports
Judging employees by results instead of hours at a desk
Giving every worker the freedom to set no hours at all
qs.why: 성공적인 회사는 관리자가 책상에 앉은 시간보다 성과를 측정하도록 교육한다고 해요.

items.title: The Thief in the East Gallery
items.text: The night guard at the small town museum, Mr. Lee, had one rule: never touch anything after closing time. On the evening of the winter festival, however, a loud crash echoed from the east gallery. His heart pounding, he grabbed his flashlight and hurried down the corridor. The beam swept across the polished floor, the glass cases, and finally a broken vase lying beneath an open window. Beside it sat a gray cat, licking its paw as if nothing had happened. Mr. Lee let out a long breath and began to laugh. He wrapped the pieces carefully in a cloth, closed the window, and carried the surprised cat to the staff room. In the morning, the director found a note on her desk: "The vase was already cracked, the window was open, and the thief is asleep in your armchair." She read it twice and smiled.

qs.q: How did Mr. Lee feel when he first heard the crash?
qs.why: 심장이 뛰는 채로 손전등을 들고 달려갔다는 데서 놀라고 긴장했음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What did Mr. Lee do after finding the broken vase?
o: He called the director and waited for her at the front gate
He chased the cat out through the open window into the garden
He searched the other galleries for a human thief all night
He gathered the pieces, shut the window, and took the cat away
qs.why: 그는 조각을 천에 싸고 창문을 닫은 뒤 고양이를 직원실로 데려갔어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about how the vase broke?
o: Mr. Lee accidentally dropped it while hurrying down the corridor
The cat most likely knocked it over after entering through the window
A visitor broke it earlier and hid it before the museum closed
It fell because the crowds at the winter festival shook the building
qs.why: 열린 창문, 깨진 꽃병 옆의 고양이, 쪽지의 '도둑' 표현에서 고양이가 원인임을 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: What is the tone of the note on the director's desk?
qs.why: 고양이를 '도둑'이라 부르는 장난스러운 표현이고, 이사는 읽고 미소 지었어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "echoed" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 큰 소리가 갤러리에 울려 퍼졌다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Singing to Remember
items.text: Many learners swear that they remember English words better when the words come with a melody. There may be good reasons. Songs repeat phrases, group them into rhythmic patterns, and connect them to emotions, all of which help memory. A teacher in a language school asked her students to learn ten common expressions in two ways: half of the class read them from a list, while the other half sang them to a simple tune. A week later, the singers recalled more of the expressions and used them more naturally in conversation. However, the teacher cautioned against drawing large conclusions from one small class. Differences in motivation, age, and prior knowledge could also have affected the results. She plans to repeat the experiment with larger groups. Meanwhile, she recommends that students try music as one tool among many, not as a replacement for regular practice.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A small experiment on learning expressions through singing
The best songs for beginners to study in English class
Why reading from a list is the worst way to study
How teachers should choose students for a class choir
qs.why: 노래로 표현을 외우는 효과를 작은 학급 실험으로 살펴보는 글이에요.

qs.q: How was the class divided in the experiment?
o: Half studied at home and half studied in class

Half read the expressions and half sang them
Half were beginners and half were advanced learners
qs.why: 절반은 목록을 읽고 나머지 절반은 간단한 곡조에 맞춰 노래했어요.

qs.q: Why does the teacher warn against large conclusions?
o: The singers forgot most of the expressions after only one week
The experiment was stopped because the school did not allow it
Other factors may have influenced the results of one small class

qs.why: 동기, 나이, 사전 지식의 차이가 결과에 영향을 줬을 수 있다고 말해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "them" in "connect them to emotions" refers to
qs.why: 노래는 구절을 반복하고 리듬으로 묶으며 감정과 연결한다는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: What is the teacher's attitude toward music in language study?

items.title: Tiny Pieces, Big Problem
items.text: Scientists use the word "microplastics" for plastic fragments smaller than five millimeters. Some are made that small on purpose, such as the beads once added to certain face scrubs. Others form slowly as larger items, including bottles, bags, and fishing nets, break down in sunlight and waves. Washing synthetic clothing also releases tiny fibers that pass through household drains. Because the pieces are so small, they are hard to remove from water, and they can be swallowed by animals at every level of the food chain, from plankton to fish. Researchers are still investigating whether the particles harm human health, and results so far are mixed. Even so, many countries have limited the sale of products containing plastic beads, and some manufacturers now sell washing machine filters that trap fibers. These steps will not solve the problem alone, but they show that practical solutions exist.

qs.q: Which of the following is a source of microplastics mentioned in the passage?
o: Natural cotton thread used for sewing
Synthetic clothing that is washed at home
Glass bottles that break on the beach
Paper bags that dissolve in the rain
qs.why: 합성 섬유 옷을 세탁하면 미세한 섬유가 나온다고 해요.

qs.q: Why are microplastics hard to remove from water?
o: They sink to the bottom of the sea
They dissolve completely in salt water
They are hidden inside fishing nets
qs.why: Because로 시작하는 문장에서 입자가 너무 작아서 제거하기 어렵다고 해요.

qs.q: What does the writer imply by saying results about human health are "mixed"?
o: Most studies have proved that the particles are harmless
Researchers refuse to study the question any further
Different countries have banned different products
Scientists have not reached a clear conclusion yet
qs.why: 연구 결과가 엇갈린다는 말은 아직 명확한 결론이 없다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "trap" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 필터가 섬유를 걸러 잡아 둔다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the last sentence?
o: To argue that the measures are a complete solution
To warn that no solution will ever be found
To show that the problem can be reduced in practical ways
To explain why researchers disagree about the problem
qs.why: 이 조치들만으로 해결되지는 않지만 현실적인 해법이 있음을 보여 주는 결론이에요.

items.title: After Dark at the Night Market
items.text: A night market is more than a place to buy dinner. As the sun sets, vendors string up lights, light their grills, and arrange their goods on narrow tables. Soon the air fills with the smell of grilled skewers, the sizzle of oil, and the calls of sellers who know their regular customers by name. Families wander slowly from stall to stall, couples share sweet pancakes, and groups of students compare the prices of phone cases. Most visitors leave with a full stomach, but what many remember is the atmosphere: the crowd, the music from a street performer, and the feeling of belonging to a place that never seems to rush. For the vendors, the market is both a livelihood and a community, and many say they would not trade it for a quiet shop with fixed hours.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Vendors earn more money at night than they do during the day
Street food is cheaper than the food in most restaurants nearby
A night market offers a lively social experience beyond shopping
Markets should close early to protect the neighborhood at night
qs.why: 단순한 저녁 식사 장소를 넘어서 분위기와 공동체를 제공하는 곳이라는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What do visitors remember most, according to the passage?
qs.why: 많은 사람들이 기억하는 것은 분위기라고 해요.

qs.q: What does the writer suggest about the vendors?
o: They are tired of selling to the same customers every night
They dislike the noise of the street performers and the crowd
They plan to open their own shops with fixed hours soon
They value the community more than a quiet, fixed schedule
qs.why: 상인들에게 시장은 생계이자 공동체이며 고정된 시간의 조용한 가게와 바꾸지 않겠다고 해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "livelihood" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 시장이 상인들에게 생계 수단이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which sentence from the passage is a general statement rather than a description of what happens in the evening?
o: "Vendors string up lights, light their grills, and arrange their goods."

"Families wander slowly from stall to stall."
qs.why: 첫 문장만 일반적인 주장이고 나머지는 저녁에 벌어지는 장면을 묘사해요.

items.title: The Helpful Mistake Machine
items.text: Most people have sent a message that autocorrect has turned into nonsense, but the feature does far more good than harm. Behind the scenes, the software compares what you type with a large list of words, estimates which word you probably meant, and replaces the error before you press send. Modern versions also learn from your habits: they remember the names of your friends, the slang you use, and the phrases you often repeat. The system is not perfect, because it cannot read your mind and it sometimes mistakes a rare word for a mistake. Experts therefore advise users to read quickly before sending any important message. They add that the tool should support careful writing, not replace it. Ironically, people who rely on it completely may notice their own spelling skills slowly weaken.

qs.q: What is the writer's main message?
o: Autocorrect should be removed from every phone and computer
Software can now read exactly what its users are thinking
Spelling skills no longer matter much in modern daily life
Autocorrect is useful, but users should still write carefully
qs.why: 자동 고침이 유용하지만 신중한 글쓰기를 대체해서는 안 된다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, how does autocorrect work?
o: It compares typed words with a list and guesses the intended word
It asks the user to check each word one by one before sending
It copies the words that the user's friends have typed before
It sends the message to language experts for their approval
qs.why: 입력한 단어를 단어 목록과 비교해 의도한 단어를 추정하고 오류를 바꿔요.

qs.q: In the passage, "it" in "people who rely on it completely" refers to
qs.why: 자동 고침 기능에 완전히 의존하는 사람들을 말해요.

qs.q: What is the function of the word "Ironically" in the last sentence?
o: It shows that the writer is making fun of every expert mentioned
It signals that a new topic is about to begin in the next paragraph
It introduces a result that is the opposite of what one would expect
It repeats the same advice that was given in the previous sentence
qs.why: 도움을 주는 도구에 의존하면 오히려 철자 실력이 약해질 수 있다는 반대되는 결과를 소개해요.

qs.q: Why does autocorrect sometimes make mistakes?
o: It cannot know exactly what the user means
It has no list of words to compare with
It forgets the names of the user's friends
It only works for messages that are short
qs.why: 사용자의 마음을 읽을 수 없고 드문 단어를 실수로 착각하기도 해서예요.

items.title: The Garden at the End of Our Street
items.text: When my family moved to the city, I missed the open fields behind our old house. The concrete, the traffic, and the crowds felt endless. Then my grandmother discovered a community garden at the end of our street. Each family there rents a small plot, and everybody shares the tools, the compost, and the knowledge. At first I only carried water cans, but soon Mr. Alvarez, the oldest gardener, taught me how to sow carrots, tie tomato plants to stakes, and tell weeds from seedlings. Over the summer I noticed that the garden gave me more than vegetables. It gave me neighbors who greeted me by name, a reason to leave my phone at home, and a quiet corner where I could think. This autumn, when we harvested our first pumpkin, my grandmother cried a little, and I understood that we had finally started to belong.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why growing vegetables is easier in the city than in the country
How the writer's grandmother became a famous gardener
Why the writer wants to move back to the old house
How a community garden helped the writer feel at home in a new city
qs.why: 새 도시에 적응하지 못하던 글쓴이가 공동체 텃밭을 통해 소속감을 찾게 된 이야기예요.

qs.q: What did Mr. Alvarez teach the writer?
o: How to rent a plot from the city office
How to sow carrots and care for tomato plants
How to cook a pumpkin for the family dinner
How to build tools for the garden
qs.why: 당근 심기, 토마토를 지지대에 묶기, 잡초와 모종 구별하기를 가르쳐 주었어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "plot" is closest in meaning to
o: the main events of a story
a secret plan to cause harm
qs.why: 가족마다 빌리는 작은 땅 한 구획을 뜻해요.

qs.q: Why did the grandmother cry a little at the harvest?
o: She was disappointed with the size of the first pumpkin
She missed the fields behind the old house they used to have
She was sad that summer was over and the nights were getting cold
The pumpkin showed that the family had begun to belong there
qs.why: 첫 호박을 수확하며 가족이 이곳에 뿌리내리기 시작했음을 느꼈다는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer imply by mentioning "a reason to leave my phone at home"?
o: The garden offered a more satisfying activity than the phone
The writer was forbidden to use a phone anywhere in the city
The phone was broken when the family moved to the new city
The grandmother disliked all modern technology in the house
qs.why: 텃밭이 휴대전화를 두고 나올 만한 이유가 되었다는 뜻이에요.
